explain.say: Colour starts with light. White light is a mix of many wavelengths, and a red apple soaks up most of them and bounces mainly the long red wavelengths into your eye.

explain.say: Your retina has about 6 million cone cells of three kinds. One kind responds most to short, bluish wavelengths, one to medium, greenish ones, and one to long, reddish ones.

explain.say: No single cone knows what colour it sees. Your brain compares how strongly each kind is firing. Strong long-wave and medium-wave signals together, with little short-wave signal, means yellow.

faq.a: Cone cells are light-sensing cells in the retina that work in bright light and give us colour and fine detail. There are three types, each most sensitive to a different range of wavelengths.
asks: What do cones in the eye do?
How many types of cone are there?

faq.q: How does the brain work out a colour?
faq.a: The brain compares the signals from the three cone types. Each colour makes a different mix: blue light mostly excites short-wave cones, while yellow excites long and medium cones together.
asks: How do three cones make all the colours?
How do we see yellow if there is no yellow cone?

faq.q: How many colours can people see?
faq.a: Scientists estimate that a person with typical colour vision can tell apart around a million different shades, all made by comparing just three cone signals.
asks: How many colours can the human eye see?
Can we see a million colours?

faq.a: In colour blindness one type of cone is missing or tuned slightly differently, so some colours look the same. The most common kind mixes up reds and greens, and it is far more common in boys and men because the genes are on the X chromosome.
asks: Why are some people colour blind?
What do colour blind people see?

faq.q: Why can't we see colours in dim light?
faq.a: Cones need fairly bright light to work. In dim light, the rod cells take over, and since there is only one type of rod, they cannot compare signals, so we see in shades of grey.
asks: Why do colours fade at night?
Why is everything grey in the dark?

facts: A human retina has about 6 million cone cells and about 120 million rod cells.
Red-green colour blindness affects about 1 in 12 men and 1 in 200 women of northern European ancestry.

quiz.say: A lemon looks yellow. Which cones are firing most strongly?
quiz.show: Looking at a yellow lemon, which cones fire most?
quiz.why: Yellow light excites both the long-wave and medium-wave cones, and the brain reads that mix as yellow.

wrong.0: Blue cones respond most to short, bluish wavelengths, not yellow.
wrong.2: In good light the cones do the colour work; rods cannot tell colours apart.
